description:
The negative assertion, and the widest record-width coverage in this folder: all SIX of CBTRN01C's declared datasets are seeded with real, deliberately RELEVANT data, and the case proves that the three the program merely opens and closes - CARDFILE, CUSTFILE and TRANFILE - contribute NOTHING WHATSOEVER to observable behaviour. The fingerprint below is byte-identical to the fingerprint of a run in which CARDFILE and CUSTFILE were empty, and that equivalence IS the assertion. Verified from source rather than assumed: app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl declares six SELECT statements at :29-62 - the most of any program in the migration - opens all six at :157-162 and closes all six at :188-193, yet the whole program contains exactly THREE READ statements, at :203 (DALYTRAN-FILE, sequential), :229 (XREF-FILE, keyed) and :243 (ACCOUNT-FILE, keyed). There is no READ CUSTOMER-FILE anywhere, no READ CARD-FILE anywhere, and TRANSACT-FILE is never read, written or rewritten - it appears only at :58 (SELECT), :91 (FD), :345 (OPEN INPUT) and :453 (CLOSE). A scan for WRITE and REWRITE across all 491 lines returns zero statements, and all six files are OPEN INPUT, so posting is not merely absent but impossible. CARDFILE is therefore seeded with carddata.txt rows 21 and 4 - the exact CARD-RECORD rows for cards 4859452612877065 (CARD-ACCT-ID 00000000007) and 0927987108636232 (CARD-ACCT-ID 00000000020) - and CUSTFILE with custdata.txt rows 7 and 20, customers 000000007 and 000000020: precisely the card and customer records a naive translation would be tempted to look up because the program declares the files. That temptation is what this case exists to catch. Practice B5 governs and is the headline here: a program that declares files it never reads is the legacy design, and it must be PRESERVED, not 'completed'. Adding a customer or card lookup - however helpful it looks next to six declared datasets and a class named TransactionPostingJob - would be a NEW FEATURE and a PARITY VIOLATION, and it fails here the moment it emits a single extra line. Read the six open paragraphs at :252-359 and the six close paragraphs at :361-467 to see why silence is the correct expectation: every one of them tests its FILE STATUS against '00' and takes CONTINUE, displaying nothing at all; only the ELSE arm displays, and no ELSE arm is reached here. So a successful open and a successful close each contribute exactly nothing, which is why seeding three more datasets adds three more pairs of file verbs and not one more message. THE TRAP, and the reason a reviewer must not read entries 6, 12 and 17 as evidence of a customer read: 'CUSTOMER ID: ' at :238 is displayed with XREF-CUST-ID, a field of the CARD-XREF-RECORD just read from the cross reference at :229 - not with anything from CUSTFILE. It is nine digits wide because app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares XREF-CUST-ID as PIC 9(09) at bytes 17-25 of a 50-byte record laid out XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) + XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) + XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) + FILLER X(14) (practice B11). A CUSTOMER ID line in this output proves only that the cross reference was read. The nineteen expected lines follow MAIN-PARA at :155-197 exactly. The loop at :164-186 runs three times for two records: twice reading '00', each time echoing the 350-byte record at :168 and then taking the NOT INVALID KEY arms at :234-238 and :248-249; and once more reading '10', which sets END-OF-DAILY-TRANS-FILE to 'Y' at :217. On that third pass the inner guard at :167 - which closes at :169 and covers ONLY the DISPLAY at :168 - suppresses the record echo, while the three statements at :170-172 and the account read at :173-179 sit OUTSIDE it and run anyway, on the DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM that row 2 left in the record area because a READ ... INTO does not disturb its receiving area AT END. Entries 14-18 are that repeat: they mirror entries 9-13 verbatim, on row 2's stale card 0927987108636232, with NO echo between entry 13 and entry 14. A run performs recordsRead + 1 lookups, always, so the count is 2 + 6n + 5 = 19 for two records; hoisting those statements inside the guard makes this case fail, which is the point. expectedWrites is EMPTY as a POSITIVE assertion that nothing was written anywhere, and the six WRITES-channel dataset expectations say the same thing per dataset at its exact copybook width, so the claim is made once globally and once per file. expectedReturnCode is stated explicitly as 0 (practice B8): CBTRN01C contains no MOVE statement targeting RETURN-CODE anywhere, APPL-RESULT transits 8 at each open seed, 0 on every '00' and 16 on the '10' at :208 without ever reaching RETURN-CODE, so normal completion is 0 and the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :473 is unreached. jobParameters is empty because CBTRN01C is the migration's ORPHAN - no EXEC PGM=CBTRN01C exists anywhere in app/jcl or app/proc - so there is no PARM for a parameter to come from and the job carries no trigger (requirement I4, gate G13). TRANFILE is declared with the empty shape rather than seeded, and the reason is recorded rather than left implicit (practice B12): TRANSACT has no fixture among the nine in app/data/ASCII, and the program neither reads nor writes it, so an explicit empty dataset carrying its width and its copybook is the only honest seed. Fabricating transaction records to fill it would invent data the repository never held (practice B1). An empty declaration is also a stronger statement than omission: omitting TRANFILE would say nothing about it, while declaring it empty asserts that a real 350-byte dataset was opened and held no row. FIVE DISTINCT RECORD WIDTHS are pinned here, more than any other case in this folder, every one taken mechanically from its copybook and every FILLER span present and space-filled (gates G19 and G21): DALYTRAN 350 from CVTRA06Y with FILLER X(20); XREFFILE 50 from CVACT03Y with FILLER X(14); ACCTFILE 300 from CVACT01Y with FILLER X(178), whose ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE keeps the copybook's own misspelling (I1); CARDFILE 150 from CVACT02Y with FILLER X(59); and CUSTFILE 500 from CVCUS01Y with FILLER X(168). TRANFILE's 350 comes from CVTRA05Y and agrees with the FD at :92-94, X(16) + X(334). The cross-reference rows are seeded at the 36 bytes the fixture actually holds and are NOT pre-padded; the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation supplies CVACT03Y's absent FILLER X(14) once, at seed time, and the final state pins all four spans by name so 16 + 9 + 11 + 14 = the whole 50 bytes and no byte goes unasserted (gate G16, risk R-F). R1 and practice B4, documented on both sides and 'fixed' on neither: the mandated class name TransactionPostingJob and the source header 'Post the records from daily transaction file' both promise posting, and the verified source posts nothing at all - the real POSTTRAN poster is CBTRN02C, which migrates as TransactionValidationJob (AAP 0.8.4). Separately: CBTRN01CParityTest once declared its own twenty cases in Java, because this resource directory was absent when the class was written. That is no longer so - cases() now returns ParityHarness.casesOf('CBTRN01C') and nothing else, so this file is the case, and the Java scenarios it diverged from have been deleted rather than left to disagree with it. The class's assertion that CBTRN01C 'never reads CUSTFILE or CARDFILE at all' is made against this case in particular, because it is the only one of the twenty that seeds all six datasets with real rows. That divergence is left visible for reconciliation instead of being silently resolved by weakening either side. Baseline provenance, practice B12: these expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl read paragraph by paragraph - :29-62 for the six SELECTs, :155-197 for the mainline and :227-250 for the two keyed lookups - cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts in app/cpy (CVTRA06Y 350, CVACT03Y 50, CVACT01Y 300, CVACT02Y 150, CVCUS01Y 500, CVTRA05Y 350) and seeded from the real ASCII fixtures: dailytran rows 1 and 2, cardxref rows 21 and 4, acctdata rows 7 and 20, carddata rows 21 and 4, custdata rows 7 and 20. They were NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, because executing it is empirically impossible in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed-file handler the available compiler reports as disabled which excludes all five ORGANIZATION INDEXED files here, and no Language Environment CEE* services, so CALL 'CEE3ABD' cannot be reached at all. AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers; the substitution changes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else, and is escalated for explicit user confirmation as risk R-A rather than silently absorbed. Bytes are US-ASCII, stated and never taken from the platform default, and nothing here reads a clock, draws an unpredictable value or consults the environment - CBTRN01C reads no clock - so the fingerprint is identical on every run (practices B7 and B8). Reference inputs were read and none was written: app/cbl, app/cpy, app/jcl and app/data are the parity oracle and stay byte-for-byte unchanged (practice B3). review_rules returns exactly one line, "No user rules provided.", and that single line is the entire document, so NO user rule governs this fixture; the binding standard is the enterprise-practice set B1-B12, and its absence is not licence to assert less. Gates carried: G13, G15, G16, G18, G19, G21, G47 (the '00' open and '00' close outcomes on all six datasets, the '00' sequential read, the '10' end-of-file that is a normal boundary rather than an error, and the NOT INVALID KEY arm at both keyed sites) and G51 (the tasklet body is driven directly, with no JobLauncher and no HTTP layer in the path). G32 does not apply: CBTRN01C contains zero GO TO statements.

THE READ SEQUENCE, DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED. expectedOperations names every read this run must issue, in order and with the key it is given, and it says three things no byte fingerprint can. First, WHICH VERB: the daily file's read is readNext because :203 reads sequentially and takes whatever record is next, while the cross reference and the account are read at :229 and :243 by a key the program built - a translation that turned either keyed read into a browse would produce identical SYSOUT. Second, HOW MANY: there is always one readNext more than there are records, because the loop at :164-186 reads again to learn it is at end of file, and the lookup that follows sits at :170-172 OUTSIDE the guard that closed at :169 - so the last lookup runs on the card number the previous record left in WORKING-STORAGE. Third, WITH WHAT: the key is recorded as declared, so on the trailing lookup it is the PREVIOUS record's card number, and on a run whose daily file was empty it is absent entirely because the record area never held anything. Every entry here was derived from this case's own expected DISPLAY lines - one echo per record at :168, one lookup block per iteration - and never from a run.
